langkah: Take the temperature with an armpit thermometer; a fever above 38°C in an infant under 3 months must be checked by a doctor.
Continue breastfeeding or formula more often to prevent dehydration.
Use thin clothing and a cool room; do not cover with thick blankets.
Apply a lukewarm compress to the forehead, neck and armpit folds for 10 15 minutes.
bayi.saran_obat: Paracetamol drops or syrup dosed by body weight ONLY on the advice of a doctor or pharmacist. Never give aspirin to a child.
bayi.red_flags: An infant under 3 months with a temperature of 38°C or higher, seizures, red spots that do not fade when pressed, persistent vomiting, or appearing very floppy and hard to wake.

langkah: Full rest and check the temperature every 4 hours.
Offer plenty of drinks: water, soup broth, or a simple oral rehydration solution.
Thin clothing, a lukewarm compress on the forehead and body folds.
Bathe in lukewarm water to help bring the temperature down.
anak.saran_obat: Paracetamol syrup dosed by body weight every 6 to 8 hours if needed. Herbal remedies such as warm turmeric with tamarind may accompany the treatment, never replace it.
anak.red_flags: Fever for more than 3 days, seizures, a purple rash, fast or difficult breathing, a child refusing to drink at all, or appearing confused.

langkah: Rest enough and sleep 7 to 8 hours so the immune system works optimally.
Drink 2 to 3 liters of water daily, supplemented with warm tea or a ginger drink.
Eat easy to digest food and vitamin C rich soups.
Compress the forehead with lukewarm water if the temperature feels high.
dewasa.saran_obat: Paracetamol 500 mg every 6 to 8 hours or ibuprofen 200 mg after meals. Warm ginger and honey with lemon help ease the accompanying symptoms.
dewasa.red_flags: A fever above 39.5°C that does not come down after medication, lasts more than 3 days, or comes with chest pain, shortness of breath, a stiff neck, or sudden blurred vision.

langkah: Monitor the temperature regularly; a fever in older adults can look mild yet signal a serious infection.
Assist with mobility to prevent falls when weak, and keep fluid intake going every 1 to 2 hours.
Use loose clothing and an environment with good air circulation.
Write down the regular medicines being taken as information for the doctor.
lansia.saran_obat: Standard dose paracetamol is generally the safest, but consult a pharmacist if the person takes blood thinners or has liver disease.
lansia.red_flags: A temperature of 38°C or higher with sudden confusion, rambling speech, extreme weakness or falls, or in people with diabetes and heart disease, take them to the emergency room immediately.

langkah: Instil 0.9% saline drops into the nose, then suction slowly with a baby nasal aspirator.
Raise the head position slightly during sleep by propping it up under the mattress.
A cool mist humidifier in the room helps loosen breathing.
Continue breastfeeding or expressed milk more often.
bayi.saran_obat: No over the counter cough medicine! For infants, saline drops and a doctor's advice are enough. Warm telon oil may be rubbed thinly on the back.
bayi.red_flags: Fast breathing or rib retractions, pulling of the chest wall, bluish lips, refusing to drink, or fever in an infant under 3 months.

langkah: Drink plenty of warm water and broth soup to thin the phlegm.
Teach blowing the nose into a tissue and washing hands afterwards.
Warm steam inhalation for 5 to 10 minutes under adult supervision.
Avoid cigarette smoke and dust inside the house.
anak.saran_obat: Children over 1 year may take 1/2 to 1 teaspoon of honey to ease a cough. Expectorant syrup only on the advice of a doctor or pharmacist.
anak.red_flags: A cough lasting more than 2 weeks, shortness of breath, an accompanying high fever, bloody phlegm, or a child who looks very weak and refuses to drink.

langkah: Rest your voice and get enough sleep.
Gargle warm salt water 3 to 4 times a day for an accompanying sore throat.
Warm fluids: ginger tea, honey lemon, soup broth.
Sleep with the head raised a little higher to reduce nasal congestion.
dewasa.saran_obat: A decongestant (pseudoephedrine) for a maximum of 3 to 5 days for blockage, antiseptic mouthwash, and steam inhalation. Ginger plus honey and lemon is comfortably effective at easing symptoms.
dewasa.red_flags: Shortness of breath, chest pain, coughing up blood, fever for more than 3 days, or symptoms that improve and then worsen again (suspected secondary infection).

langkah: Keep the body and the room warm, avoiding direct cold air.
Drink warm fluids regularly to thin thick secretions.
Sit leaning forward during severe coughing fits to avoid falling.
Monitor oxygen saturation if you own a home oximeter.
lansia.saran_obat: Take care with decongestants in people with high blood pressure and glaucoma, consult a pharmacist first. Paracetamol is safe for the accompanying body aches.
lansia.red_flags: Saturation below 93%, fast breathing, confusion, pale or bluish lips, or a cough with high fever, pneumonia risk is high in older adults, go to the emergency room immediately.

langkah: Continue breastfeeding without limit; for formula fed babies continue as usual (do not dilute it).
Give oral rehydration solution in small sips (one spoon every 1 to 2 minutes) after every loose stool.
Change the diaper immediately and clean the area with running water to prevent rash.
Watch for signs of dehydration: a sunken soft spot, crying without tears.
bayi.saran_obat: Oral rehydration solution plus zinc 10 mg/day for 10 days (infant dose) as directed by a doctor. Never give adult anti diarrhea drugs to an infant.
bayi.red_flags: Bloody or mucous stools, projectile vomiting, refusing to drink, sunken eyes or soft spot, no urination for more than 6 hours, or age under 6 months.

langkah: Give oral rehydration solution after every loose stool (half to one glass).
Eat small portions: porridge, banana, double cooked rice; avoid fatty and high sugar food.
Wash hands with soap after using the toilet and before eating.
Rest at home until free of loose stools for 24 hours.
anak.saran_obat: Oral rehydration solution and zinc 20 mg/day for 10 days. Probiotic yogurt may support the recovery of gut flora.
anak.red_flags: High fever with diarrhea, bloody stools, a child who looks very weak or drowsy, signs of dehydration (very dry mouth, no urination for more than 8 hours).

langkah: Rehydrate: oral rehydration solution, coconut water, soup broth, avoid coffee and soda.
The BRAT diet (banana, rice, applesauce, toast) for the first 1 to 2 days.
Avoid spicy food, fatty food and fresh milk while the symptoms last.
Wash hands regularly so it does not spread to household members.
dewasa.saran_obat: Oral rehydration solution is the priority. Attapulgite may be used for diarrhea without blood or fever. Probiotics and a ginger decoction help calm the gut.
dewasa.red_flags: Diarrhea for more than 3 days, black or bloody stools, fever above 38.5°C, vomiting without end so no fluid stays down, signs of severe dehydration (dizziness when standing).

langkah: Give oral rehydration solution immediately, dehydration in older adults deteriorates fast and causes confusion.
Help them to the toilet to prevent falls during weakness or stomach cramps.
Eat warm soft food: thin mung bean porridge, carrot soup.
Stop laxatives and certain supplements only after consulting a doctor.
lansia.saran_obat: Oral rehydration solution is mandatory. Avoid loperamide in older adults without supervision (risk of heart rhythm disorders and ileus). Probiotics are safe and helpful.
lansia.red_flags: An older adult who looks confused or delirious, an extremely dry mouth, no urination for more than 8 hours, fever, or bloody diarrhea, this is an emergency, go to the emergency room.

langkah: Infants cannot complain yet; suspect it from behavior: excessive fussiness, banging the head, refusing to feed.
Check for a recent immunization or fever, often the main source of head discomfort.
Dim the lights and noise, hold and rock gently.
Measure the body temperature immediately.
bayi.saran_obat: There is no over the counter headache medicine for infants. Treat the cause (fever leads to paracetamol drops at the doctor's dose). A mother's touch and voice are the best relievers.
bayi.red_flags: Fussiness that cannot be soothed for more than 3 hours, seizures, a bulging soft spot, projectile vomiting, or one occurring after a head bump or trauma.

langkah: Rest in a dim, quiet room away from screens for 30 60 minutes.
Offer a drink, mild dehydration is a common trigger in active children.
Gently massage the temples and the back of the neck with warm oil.
Check for eye strain from watching screens or playing with devices too long.
anak.saran_obat: Paracetamol syrup at the right dose if the child is in pain. A cold forehead compress and warm chamomile tea help.
anak.red_flags: Headaches on waking that become more frequent day by day, with vomiting, disturbed vision or strength, a stiff neck, or high fever.

langkah: Recognize the type: tightness around the whole head (tension) versus one throbbing side (migraine).
Reduce screen time, control your breathing, massage the temples and nape for 5 minutes.
Drink water, dehydration and skipped meals are the most frequent triggers.
A cold forehead compress for migraine; a warm neck compress for the tension type.
dewasa.saran_obat: Paracetamol or ibuprofen 200 to 400 mg at the start of an attack. A little sweet coffee or tea actually helps in an early migraine. Ginger effectively relieves migraine nausea.
dewasa.red_flags: The worst headache ever felt, arriving suddenly (thunderclap), with one sided weakness, slurred speech, seizures, double vision, or fever plus a stiff neck.

langkah: Check blood pressure during head pain, hypertension often has no symptom besides an ache at the back of the head.
Get out of bed slowly to prevent orthostatic dizziness.
Rest with a slightly higher pillow and avoid rooms that are too dark.
Note when and where the pain appears, to report it to the doctor.
lansia.saran_obat: Paracetamol is the safest. Avoid caffeine combination medicines if the older adult has high blood pressure or tachycardia. Do not overuse headache medicine (more than 15 days per month).
lansia.red_flags: A new headache never experienced before in someone over 50, with sudden blurred vision, jaw pain when chewing, one sided weakness, or sudden confusion.

langkah: A true nosebleed is rare in infants, check for any wound or impact around the nose.
Pinch the soft part of the nose with a clean soft cloth for 5 to 10 minutes, holding the baby half sitting.
Do not put tissue or dry cotton into a baby's nostril.
Breastfeed to calm them.
bayi.saran_obat: No medicine is needed. Warm steam in the room keeps the nasal lining from drying out and cracking.
bayi.red_flags: Bleeding that does not stop after 10 minutes of pressure, bleeding after a head injury, or bleeding with unexplained bruises elsewhere on the body.

langkah: Sit upright with the head TILTED SLIGHTLY FORWARD (not backward, so no blood is swallowed).
Gently pinch the soft part of the nose for a full 10 minutes without releasing to check.
A cold compress on the bridge of the nose.
After it stops, remind the child not to pick the nose or blow hard for 24 hours.
anak.saran_obat: A thin layer of petroleum ointment inside the nostril before sleep prevents a dry lining. Saline nasal spray also helps.
anak.red_flags: Does not stop after 20 minutes, happens very often, the child turns pale or weak, or there is a history of clotting disorders and easy bruising.

langkah: Pinch the soft part of the nose for 10 15 minutes while sitting leaning forward, breathing through the mouth.
An ice pack wrapped in cloth on the bridge of the nose.
Avoid bending down, lifting heavy items, and spicy or hot food for 24 hours.
Keep the room humid with a humidifier.
dewasa.saran_obat: A decongestant nasal spray (oxymetazoline) once or twice can help stop an episode in adults, but never for more than 3 days. Use saline spray for prevention.
dewasa.red_flags: Heavy bleeding that does not stop after 20 minutes, a nosebleed after head or face trauma, or nosebleeds in people taking blood thinners, go to the emergency room immediately.

langkah: Sit upright and pinch the soft part of the nose for 15 minutes, older blood vessels need pressure longer.
Check blood pressure after the bleeding stops.
Avoid letting glasses press on the nose for a while.
Apply a thin layer of petroleum jelly inside the nose when the night air is dry.
lansia.saran_obat: Aspirin or warfarin users risk bleeding that is hard to stop, report every nosebleed to the prescribing doctor. Do not stop the medicine on your own.
lansia.red_flags: Does not stop after 20 minutes of pressure, blood flowing heavily down the throat, dizziness or fainting, or while taking blood thinners, go to the emergency room.

langkah: Suspect colic when the baby screams and is fussy in the evening or at night with a bloated belly, usually between 2 and 12 weeks of age.
Burp the baby after feeding, then hold them face down on your arm or over your tummy.
Gentle bicycle leg movements to help pass gas.
Massage the tummy clockwise with warm baby oil.
bayi.saran_obat: Infant simethicone drops only on a doctor's advice. A little warm water for babies over 6 months is fine as a companion to complementary food.
bayi.red_flags: A hard bloated belly, green or brownish vomit, no stool and no gas, crying when the belly is touched, or a groin lump that cannot be pushed back in.

langkah: Rest with the knees bent toward the chest to reduce cramps.
Give warm water in small sips, and avoid soda and cold food or drinks.
Ask where it hurts: around the navel is usually mild; pain moving to the lower right needs caution.
A gentle warm compress on the belly.
anak.saran_obat: Avoid strong stomach pain relievers in children without a doctor's advice. Warm chamomile tea and eucalyptus oil rubbed on the belly help.
anak.red_flags: Pain that persists for more than 8 hours, moves to the lower right abdomen with fever or vomiting (suspected appendicitis), a hard belly, bloody stools, or a child who looks very weak.

langkah: Recognize the pattern: burning tied to meals means gastritis or GERD; cramps plus loose stools mean mild diarrhea or colitis.
Eat small regular portions, and avoid spicy, sour, coconut milk dishes and coffee while symptoms last.
Manage stress, the gut brain axis really does trigger functional abdominal pain.
A warm belly compress plus warm ginger tea relieves cramps.
dewasa.saran_obat: Antacid for the burning of gastritis, simethicone for bloating. Turmeric and galangal traditionally help with mild stomach inflammation.
dewasa.red_flags: Severe pain concentrated at one point and getting worse, high fever, vomiting blood or black stools, a belly as hard as a board, or lower right abdominal pain (suspected appendicitis).

langkah: Abdominal pain in older adults more often reflects a serious problem, have it assessed earlier.
Note the location, duration and triggers (food, bowel movements, activity).
Eat soft food in small portions and avoid over the counter NSAID painkillers.
Check whether stool or gas cannot pass at all (suspected bowel obstruction).
lansia.saran_obat: Common antacids are safe. Watch for drug interactions: NSAIDs such as mefenamic acid can worsen gastritis and ulcers in older adults.
lansia.red_flags: Sudden severe abdominal pain, a hard bloated belly with no gas passed, continuous vomiting, chest pain spreading into the abdomen, or bloody stools, go to the emergency room immediately.
